classification.difficultyReason: Choose the negative quotient giving a nonnegative remainder, then construct two related number-line classes across negative and positive values; the scaffold links the representations.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Write $-13$ as a multiple of 5 plus remainder, where the remainder is 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4.

answer.worked:
$5\times(-3)=-15$, which is the multiple of 5 immediately below $-13$.

$$-13=5\times(-3)+2$$

The remainder is 2.
From part a, division by 5 leaves remainder 2, so $-13\equiv2\pmod{5}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Mark the multiples of 5 between $-26$ and 14 on a number line. Mark also $-13$ and all integers between $-26$ and 14 congruent to $-13$ modulo 5.

answer.worked:
Mark the multiples of 5 at intervals of 5. Since $-13\equiv2\pmod{5}$, mark the integers 2 units to the right of these multiples:

$$-23,-18,-13,-8,-3,2,7,12.$$

These include $-13$; adjacent marked integers differ by 5.
